The art of perfecting the Bonsai tree: a life long pursuit of creating and maintaining the most perfect and personally pleasing object you can. It must be grown and shaped with careful planning over years of time. A single mistake can mean ruinage or failure, as it can take months or years to see your efforts take shape. It takes constant trimming, modification, and maintenance.

It looks subtly innocent and simple, but slight changes can mean very different outcomes. It also teaches acceptance, because not every flaw can be corrected, nor can it ever achieve what you want to perfection, not if you spend your time contemplating its structure.

And forgive what happens when you see another you find more pleasing. Not to mention that care is something that can be difficult. You learn to water it, but question the watering and change it, just to see that it is not as healthy, or you re-pot it and find that it doesn't like the soil. You change lighting, temperature, sound, location, all seem to have an effect on this small, simple object.

The universe forgive if you forget to care for it, the repercussions can be detrimental to years of work. The Bonsai tree is a life-long project of perfection that can never come. It teaches you patience, planning, care, and acceptance. The Bonsai tree is a life-long struggle/fail situation. It might not be exciting in the traditional sense, but the effort is never dull.

Bonsai trees are like a form of meditation, you free your mind of outside things and focus on the needs of the tree and what needs to be done to help it become what it can. It's an act of unselfishness and focus that makes you look at the world a little different. It gifts you time for your unconscious to take over and unload and think about things. Nothing like de-stressing from a day while you wrap, and trim, and plan, and study what can make it better. Such a simple hobby with so many benefits.
